summary: Alignment workshop to finalize POC success criteria, go/no-go thresholds, and reporting format. Agreed core acceptance metrics (latency p95, token cost, accuracy for reranker), trial data deliverables, and a timeline for benchmarking + final decision meeting. Security questions to be surfaced; Redwood to provide benchmark template and perf matrix.
transcript: 00:00 Lena Park (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, looks like we have a full room. We'll run ~50 minutes, confirm objectives to lock the POC acceptance rules. 00:12 Jordan (PM): Thanks Lena, excited. quick background, we want to replace our current re-rank pipeline and export latency improvements plus cost reduction. 00:30 Marcus (SE): Great, can you say current baseline numbers, p95 and cost per 1k tokens? 00:37 Jordan: Right now p95 is around 420ms for the re-ranker in prod, cost is roughly $0.12 per 1k tokens because we're on older model family and single-A100 nodes. 00:49 Samir (SRE): Also note our 90th percentile memory spike during batch runs causes retries occasionally. 00:55 Marcus: ok that's useful. for the POC we usually ask for a 24h traffic sample and a representative prompt corpus, that way our benchmark is realistic. 01:05 Jordan: Yep we'll share that, maybe obfuscated. 01:12 Nina (Security): obfuscation is necessary, we have PHI-ish fields. we want KMS integration, and we need to see audit logs. 01:20 Lena: Understood — Redwood Private supports customer KMS and audit logs; we'll include the security brief. 01:26 Nina: also SAML SSO and RBAC for console, plus retention controls. 01:32 Marcus: Yep we support SSO and RBAC policies; retention is configurable per tenant. 01:40 Arun (DS): on metrics, besides latency and cost we want NDC/accuracy change for top-5 rerank position — like NDCG@5 delta relative to current model. 01:50 Marcus: Good call. propose primary acceptance metrics: p95 latency under 250ms (hosted) or under 350ms (private with KV cache warm), token cost under $0.03 per 1k tokens for our chosen model/quantization, and NDCG@5 delta >= 0 (no degradation) with target +5% uplift desirable. 02:12 Jordan: Those sound reasonable but 250ms is aggressive for our workloads. Can we do a staged acceptance? 02:19 Lena: Absolutely — we'll define Go/Conditional Go/No-Go tiers. Go = meets all primary thresholds; Conditional Go = meets latency and cost but minor quality regression that is acceptable within defined tolerance; No-Go = any critical security gating or >5% quality regression. 02:37 Samir: What about throughput? our peak concurrency is ~600 qps during flash events. 02:43 Marcus: We will size benchmark cluster to replicate 75% and 100% peaks. For POC we run sample 75% and a high-concurrency stress run. We'll report tokens/sec and comp-latency distribution. 02:56 Jordan: ok timeline? 03:00 Lena: Here's a proposed timeline: share template and perf matrix by Oct 1, Atlas shares data by Oct 2, Redwood runs smoke baseline the week Oct 5-9, full benchmark Oct 12-16, Go/No-Go review Oct 19. does that align? 03:16 Jordan: Oct 19 is fine. 03:19 Nina: note we need SOC2 artifact review before we do private cluster. 03:24 Lena: We'll attach SOC2 scope and encryption docs in the security packet. 03:30 Arun: For reporting format, we need CSV + dashboard screenshots and a 1-page executive summary with clear pass/fail flags and observed variability. 03:40 Marcus: We typically produce a zipped report: CSV of raw trace, perf summary table (p50/p90/p95/p99), cost estimate per million tokens, NDCG/accuracy tables, and a slides PDF with recommendations. We'll adapt to your columns. 03:54 Jordan: Good — can you include a simple A/B comparison to our baseline row-by-row? 03:59 Marcus: yes, we'll include diff columns and a delta NDCG, and we'll highlight regressions >2% in red. 04:06 Samir: Network constraints — smoke tests will be done from private VPC; we need IPs for allowlist. 04:11 Lena: We'll provide a list and coordinate with your infra lead. 04:15 Nina: encryption at rest + in flight are musts; any key handling? 04:20 Marcus: We support customer-managed KMS; keys never leave your KMS for Private; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys and optional BYOK for enterprise. 04:35 Jordan: On quantization — we saw different accuracy tradeoffs. how are you going to present the variants? 04:40 Marcus: We'll run three quantization profiles: fp16 baseline, int8 dynamic, and q4_0 approximate. For each we'll show latency/cost/accuracy. 04:51 Arun: Can you also include GPU utilization traces and KV cache hit rate? those matter for our ops. 04:57 Marcus: yes KV cache warmup behavior and hit rate time series will be included. 05:04 Lena: ok let's formalize the go/no-go thresholds here for the record: 05:08 Lena: Go = p95 <= 250ms (hosted) OR p95 <= 350ms (private with warm cache), cost <= $0.03 per 1k tokens, NDCG@5 delta >= 0, no open critical security issues. 05:23 Lena: Conditional Go = latency or cost slightly above (latency up to +20%) but quality within tolerance (NDCG drop <= 2%) and remediation plan accepted. 05:36 Lena: No-Go = NDCG drop > 5% OR any unmet compliance gating OR sustained instability during stress runs (error rate >1%). 05:48 Jordan: Sounds fair. can we add a small SLA on response variance — e.g., p99 spikes not > 2x baseline? 05:56 Marcus: We'll include p99 spike watch and mark as informational threshold; if p99 > 2x baseline we flag and require mitigation but it won't automatically be No-Go unless it's causing user-visible errors. 06:10 Nina: For reporting columns, include: timestamp, request_id, latency_ms, model_variant, quant_profile, kv_cache_hit, cpu/gpu_util_percent, tokens_generated, ndcg5, cost_estimate_usd. 06:28 Marcus: noted. We'll send a template CSV with those headers. 06:33 Jordan: For decision meeting, who should attend? we want PM, SRE, security, and an ops person. 06:39 Lena: We'll have AE+SE and a solutions engineer; Marcus will present runbook and results. 06:44 Samir: If we need to execute on-prem tests, lead time for procurement is ~2 weeks. 06:50 Lena: We'll aim to use Redwood Dedicated hosted runs first to accelerate. if you need Private, we can schedule private cluster provisioning in parallel. 06:58 Jordan: budget sensitivity — what if cost estimate is higher than forecast? 07:03 Lena: We'll show per-variant cost and a recommended config to meet your budget. also discuss burst throttling and hybrid routing to cheaper model variants during peaks. 07:12 Arun: Any risks you foresee? 07:15 Marcus: main risk is data mismatch leading to accuracy regressions; second is network egress causing apparent latency. 07:21 Nina: on compliance, we need to run through data retention policy and deletion guarantees. 07:26 Lena: we'll include a one-pager on retention and deletion flows. 07:31 Jordan: Can you explicitly mark which thresholds are subjective vs hard gate? 07:35 Lena: yes — we'll produce a Go/Conditional Go/No-Go rubric table in the report. 07:40 Marcus: we'll also include sample SQL to compute NDCG@5 so you can reproduce. 07:46 Jordan: ok next steps recap? 07:49 Lena: I'll go through those: 1) send benchmark template + example rows (Oct 1) 2) Atlas share 24h sample (Oct 2) 3) smoke baseline run (week of Oct 5) 4) full benchmark (Oct 12-16) 5) decision review (Oct 19). 08:09 Jordan: good, please include estimated cost delta scenarios in the report. 08:13 Marcus: will do. 08:15 Nina: final Q — auditing: can you provide an attested list of sub-processors? 08:20 Lena: yes that's in the security packet. 08:23 Jordan: Great thanks everyone. 08:26 Speaker 3: (inaudible) 08:30 Lena: we'll follow up with calendar invite for Oct 19 for the decision meeting and drop the files. appreciate all the clarity. 08:37 Jordan: thanks all, bye. 08:40 meeting end: transcript stops.
